issues.legal_issue: A successful execution-auction bidder satisfies the required initial and balance payments when the initial portion is paid with reasonable speed in the circumstances and the balance is paid within the prescribed period.
material_facts: The successful bidder provided drafts for the required initial portion on the day the auction was completed, and the court auctioneer recorded receipt of them.
The bidder deposited the remaining portion within the prescribed period.
The initial payment was made by drafts rather than cash at the fall of the hammer.
issues.conclusion: The bidder complied with the payment requirements, and the auction sale was properly confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21 Rules 84 and 85 of the Code of Civil Procedure require payment of the initial portion immediately and the balance within the prescribed period. In Rosali V. v. Talco Bank, AIR 2007 SC 998, the Court held that “immediately” means with all reasonable speed in light of the circumstances, not necessarily instantaneously. Applying that construction, payment by drafts on the auction day was sufficient in this case.

predicates.execution_auction: The property was sold through an auction conducted to execute a court decree.
predicates.bidder_paid_initial_share_with_reasonabl: The successful bidder paid the required initial portion with reasonable speed in the circumstances of the auction.
predicates.bidder_paid_balance_within_required_peri: The successful bidder paid the remaining portion within the period required for payment.

issues.definition: When a property is sold in an execution auction, payment of the initial portion with reasonable speed and payment of the balance within the required period mean that the auction payment requirements are satisfied.

issues.legal_issue: A judgment debtor seeking to set aside an execution sale must make the required deposits within the applicable period, and an application without those deposits cannot prevent confirmation of the sale.
material_facts: A judgment debtor applied to set aside the execution sale before the sale was confirmed.
The application did not include the deposits required to set aside the sale, and the judgment debtor did not make those deposits within the applicable period.
The judgment debtor later offered to pay the auction purchaser’s amount, with interest and an additional sum, after the applicable period had passed.
issues.conclusion: The application could not be entertained without the required timely deposits; the sale could not be set aside on the basis of the application, the later offer was rejected, and the confirmed sale was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21 Rule 89 CPC requires the judgment debtor to deposit the amount payable to the decree-holder and five per cent of the purchase money for the auction purchaser. The deposit is a condition precedent and must be unconditional and made within the applicable period. Order 21 Rule 92(2), read with Article 127 of the Limitation Act, provides for the relevant period; Jammulu Ramulu, (2001) 7 SCC 71, held that Rule 92(2) does not itself prescribe a separate limitation period for the deposit and that a deposit made within the application period may be considered, subject to the court’s discretion where applicable. The Court also relied on Tribhovandas Purshottamdas Thakkar, AIR 1968 SC 372, and Challamane Huchha Gowda v. M. R. Tirumala, (2004) 1 SCC 453, on the purpose of Rule 89 as a final opportunity to save the property by satisfying the decree-holder and compensating the purchaser. The required deposits were not made within the applicable period, so the application could not be allowed.

predicates.execution_sale: The property was sold through a court process to enforce a decree.
predicates.judgment_debtor_sought_to_set_aside_sale: The judgment debtor asked the court to set aside the execution sale.
predicates.required_deposits_not_made_within_applic: The judgment debtor did not make the required payments within the period applicable to the request to set aside the sale.

issues.definition: If a judgment debtor seeks to set aside an execution sale but does not make the required deposits within the applicable period, the sale cannot be set aside on that application.
